title.es: Leer el ambiente de la conversación

es: Reconocer aperturas, señales de interés, cambios de tema y cierres en conversaciones informales entre desconocidos, e inferir por el tono y las pistas si alguien quiere seguir hablando.

teaching.en: 'What brought you to the book fair tonight?' is a safe opener, because it asks about the shared context and never feels like an interrogation.
teaching.es: «¿Qué te trajo esta noche a la feria del libro?» es una apertura segura, porque pregunta por el contexto compartido y nunca parece un interrogatorio.
teaching.explanationEs: Un opener pregunta por algo que ambos ven o viven: es ligero y fácil de contestar.
segments: 'What brought you to the book fair tonight?' is a safe opener, because
it asks about the shared context and never feels like an interrogation.
teaching.audioText: 'What brought you to the book fair tonight?' is a safe opener, because it asks about the shared context and never feels like an interrogation.

teaching.en: At a wedding you mingle for hours, so you will often strike up a conversation with an acquaintance of the couple and exchange pleasantries about the venue first.
teaching.es: En una boda socializas durante horas, así que a menudo entablarás conversación con un conocido de la pareja y empezarás intercambiando cortesías sobre el local.
teaching.explanationEs: Strike up a conversation = empezarla con alguien; pleasantries son comentarios corteses sin compromiso.
segments: At a wedding you mingle for hours, so you will often strike up a
conversation with an acquaintance of the couple and exchange pleasantries about the venue first.
teaching.audioText: At a wedding you mingle for hours, so you will often strike up a conversation with an acquaintance of the couple and exchange pleasantries about the venue first.

teaching.en: She sounded genuine when she answered, 'Oh, really? How did that happen?', whereas a listener who only murmurs 'Right' gives you nothing to build on.
teaching.es: Sonaba sincera cuando respondió: «¿Ah, sí? ¿Cómo pasó eso?», mientras que quien solo murmura «Ya» no te da nada sobre lo que continuar.
teaching.explanationEs: El interés genuino se oye en el eco y en la pregunta de detalle; el desinterés, en respuestas secas.
segments: She sounded genuine when she answered, 'Oh, really? How did that happen?', whereas
a listener who only murmurs 'Right' gives you nothing to build on.
teaching.audioText: She sounded genuine when she answered, 'Oh, really? How did that happen?', whereas a listener who only murmurs 'Right' gives you nothing to build on.

teaching.en: A one-word answer followed by a quick glance at the phone is a cue that the person wants to leave, so learn to read the room before you start a long story.
teaching.es: Una respuesta de una palabra seguida de una mirada rápida al móvil es una señal de que la persona quiere irse, así que aprende a captar el ambiente antes de empezar una historia larga.
teaching.explanationEs: Cue es una pista; read the room significa interpretar el estado de ánimo del grupo.
segments: A one-word answer followed by a quick glance at the phone is a cue that the
person wants to leave, so learn to read the room before you start a long story.
teaching.audioText: A one-word answer followed by a quick glance at the phone is a cue that the person wants to leave, so learn to read the room before you start a long story.

teaching.en: If the conversation turns awkward, steer it back to something neutral, such as the food or the music, instead of pressing on with the same subject.
teaching.es: Si la conversación se vuelve incómoda, reconduce hacia algo neutro, como la comida o la música, en lugar de insistir con el mismo tema.
teaching.explanationEs: Steer it back = volver con suavidad a un tema cómodo; no hace falta explicar el silencio.
segments: If the conversation turns awkward, steer it back to something neutral, such as
the food or the music, instead of pressing on with the same subject.
teaching.audioText: If the conversation turns awkward, steer it back to something neutral, such as the food or the music, instead of pressing on with the same subject.

teaching.en: A warm closing is brief and gives a reason, as in 'It was great chatting, but I'll let you get back to your friends,' and only skilled listeners pick up on it.
teaching.es: Un cierre cálido es breve y da un motivo, como en «Fue genial charlar, pero te dejo volver con tus amigos», y solo los buenos oyentes lo captan.
teaching.explanationEs: El cierre agradece, justifica y no se alarga; pick up on = darse cuenta de algo que no se dice abiertamente.
segments: A warm closing is brief and gives a reason, as in 'It was great chatting, but
I'll let you get back to your friends,' and only skilled listeners pick up on it.
teaching.audioText: A warm closing is brief and gives a reason, as in 'It was great chatting, but I'll let you get back to your friends,' and only skilled listeners pick up on it.

prompt.es: Clasifica lo que dice un desconocido a otro visitante de la feria.

choices.text: A cue of genuine interest in a detail she just gave
An opener that uses something both people can see
A closing that gives a polite reason to leave

feedback.es: Nadie ha hablado aún: el desconocido arranca con un objeto compartido (el libro) y una pregunta fácil, lo propio de una apertura.

hint.es: Fíjate en si ya había una conversación antes de esa frase.

origin.text: At the book fair, a stranger beside the coffee stall turns to a woman and says: 'I couldn't help noticing you've picked up the same novel I've been looking for all year. Is it any good?'

prompt.es: Completa: «Era una señal clara de que quería terminar la conversación.»

feedback.es: Cue es la pista o señal que revela lo que alguien siente sin decirlo; aquí, las respuestas de una sola sílaba y la mirada a la puerta.

hint.es: Es una pista que te ayuda a leer la situación.

origin.text: Mia answered in single syllables, looked down at her phone and glanced at the door. It was a clear ___ that she wanted the conversation to end.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Me encantaría saber más, pero te dejo que sigas socializando.»

answer.text: I'd love to hear more, but I'll let you mingle

feedback.es: La despedida cálida combina el interés («I'd love to hear more») con un motivo para cerrar («I'll let you mingle»).

hint.es: Empieza por el deseo y termina con el motivo para cerrar.

prompt.es: Escucha el relato y elige qué señal llevó a la narradora a marcharse.

choices.text: He started talking about the cake instead of the flat.
He said he had to go back to the rest of his family.
His replies got shorter while he kept looking at his phone.

feedback.es: Las respuestas cada vez más cortas y las miradas al móvil son las señales que la narradora dice haber captado antes de despedirse.

origin.audio: At my cousin's wedding I ended up at a table next to a man I had never met. I opened with a simple question about how he knew the bride, and he said they had once shared a flat in college. I repeated his words, six people in one flat, and he laughed and told me the whole story. Ten minutes later, though, he began checking his phone, and his answers got shorter and shorter. I took the hint, thanked him for the story and went off to find the cake.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase de una boda con su función en la conversación.

pairs: What brought you to the book fair tonight?
Six languages? How did you manage that?
Speaking of food, have you tried the cake?
I'll let you mingle, it was lovely talking to you.

feedback.es: Cada frase lleva su marca: pregunta de contexto, eco con detalle, enlace «Speaking of…» y despedida con motivo y buenos deseos.

pairs: What brought you to the book fair tonight?
Six languages? How did you manage that?
Speaking of food, have you tried the cake?
I'll let you mingle, it was lovely talking to you.

prompt.es: Decide qué función cumple la frase de esta invitada al entrar en la sala.

choices.text: An opener that mentions a shared situation and invites a reply
A change of topic that moves away from something they were discussing
A closing that thanks the listener and gives a reason to leave

feedback.es: No había conversación previa: la invitada abre con una observación compartida y una pregunta con humor que pide respuesta.

origin.text: A guest approaches another guest she has never spoken to, nods towards the dance floor and says: 'You've been standing by the window for a while. Are you waiting for someone, or hiding from the dancing like I am?'

prompt.es: Escucha el recuerdo de Tom y elige qué se deduce del final de la charla.

choices.text: She felt offended by his question about what had surprised her most.
She enjoyed the chat but used the talk as a polite exit.
She wanted to keep talking but could not find her friends in time.

feedback.es: Tras responder con calidez a sus preguntas, ella mira el reloj y alega la charla y sus amigos: un cierre cortés, no un enfado.

origin.audio: Tom recalls a conversation at the book fair. The woman beside him said she had been writing novels for thirty years. He replied, thirty years? That must take patience, and she smiled and told him about her first book. He asked what had surprised her most about the job. She paused, looked at her watch and said she should really find her friends before the talk began. Tom laughed it off, but he never saw her again.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige con qué fin repite Tom «thirty years?».

choices.text: To doubt that her claim could possibly be true.
To move the subject on to her first book.
To show interest and invite her to say more.

feedback.es: Repetir el dato y añadir «That must take patience» es un eco admirado: ella responde contando su primer libro, es decir, amplía.

origin.audio: Tom recalls a conversation at the book fair. The woman beside him said she had been writing novels for thirty years. He replied, thirty years? That must take patience, and she smiled and told him about her first book. He asked what had surprised her most about the job. She paused, looked at her watch and said she should really find her friends before the talk began. Tom laughed it off, but he never saw her again.

prompt.es: Completa: «No supo captar las señales de que ella había dejado de escuchar.»

feedback.es: Pick up on significa darse cuenta de algo que no se dice abiertamente, como una señal de desinterés.

origin.text: Mia was standing by the wall, looking at her messages. Tom kept talking, but he failed to ___ up on the signs that she had stopped listening.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Intercambiaron cortesías antes de pasar a algo más personal.»

answer.text: They exchanged pleasantries before moving on to something more personal

feedback.es: Pleasantries son las cortesías iniciales; la secuencia «before moving on to» marca el paso a un tema más personal.

prompt.es: Lee el mensaje de Leo y elige qué actitud transmite hacia Ana.

choices.text: Honest and a little worried, yet keen to talk again.
Offended that she showed so little interest in his stories.
Careless about whether the evening went well for her.

feedback.es: Leo reconoce que habla mucho, se pregunta si se alargó demasiado y aun así propone seguir otro día: autocrítica con ganas de repetir.

origin.text: Dear Ana, thank you for a lovely evening. I hope I didn't keep you too long: I tend to talk a lot when I'm nervous. I noticed you kept glancing towards the food table, so I wonder whether I talked for too long. Either way, it was lovely to meet you, and I'd enjoy hearing the end of your story some other time.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué hace el hablante con «enough about me».

choices.text: He ends the chat politely and heads for the exit.
He stops talking about himself and hands the turn over.
He changes the subject because he prefers another topic.

feedback.es: Se disculpa por haber hablado tanto y devuelve el turno con una pregunta abierta: reequilibra la charla, no la cierra.

origin.audio: I'm so sorry, I've been going on about my search for a flat for ages. Enough about me! Are you here for the talk, or just browsing the stalls?

prompt.es: Completa: «Lo más fácil es entablar conversación comentando algo que todos ven.»

feedback.es: Strike up a conversation es la colocación para iniciarla con alguien que no conoces, a menudo con un comentario sobre lo compartido.

origin.text: Nobody at the table knew each other, and the silence was getting heavy. The easiest way to ___ up a conversation is to comment on something you can all see, like the music.

es: Presentarse en pocas frases con un dato memorable y una pregunta que abra conversación, y usar coletillas (con entonación ascendente o descendente) para buscar acuerdo o información.

teaching.en: A bland introduction that gives only your name and job title is forgettable, because ten other guests at the venue said exactly the same thing.
teaching.es: Una presentación sosa que solo da tu nombre y tu cargo se olvida enseguida, porque otros diez invitados del local dijeron exactamente lo mismo.
teaching.explanationEs: Bland describe algo sin sabor; forgettable es lo contrario de memorable; venue es el lugar del evento.
segments: A bland introduction that gives only your name and job title is forgettable,
because ten other guests at the venue said exactly the same thing.
teaching.audioText: A bland introduction that gives only your name and job title is forgettable, because ten other guests at the venue said exactly the same thing.

teaching.en: To stand out, add a hook: 'I'm Sara, a nurse who is learning to surf at forty,' which gives people something concrete to remember.
teaching.es: Para destacar, añade un gancho: «Soy Sara, enfermera, y estoy aprendiendo a hacer surf a los cuarenta», que da a la gente algo concreto que recordar.
teaching.explanationEs: El hook es un dato concreto y sorprendente que se queda en la memoria; stand out = destacar.
segments: To stand out, add a hook: 'I'm Sara, a nurse who is
learning to surf at forty,' which gives people something concrete to remember.
teaching.audioText: To stand out, add a hook: 'I'm Sara, a nurse who is learning to surf at forty,' which gives people something concrete to remember.

teaching.en: One small quirk makes you memorable, such as 'I bake bread at five every morning', and a witty detail works better than a list of qualifications.
teaching.es: Una pequeña rareza te hace memorable, como «Hago pan a las cinco de la mañana», y un detalle ingenioso funciona mejor que una lista de títulos.
teaching.explanationEs: Quirk es un hábito peculiar y simpático; witty es con ingenio, sin ser un chiste forzado.
segments: One small quirk makes you memorable, such as 'I bake bread at five
every morning', and a witty detail works better than a list of qualifications.
teaching.audioText: One small quirk makes you memorable, such as 'I bake bread at five every morning', and a witty detail works better than a list of qualifications.

teaching.en: Keep the pitch short, avoid jargon that only your colleagues understand, and finish with a question that hands the floor back: 'I design gardens. What about you?'
teaching.es: Mantén la presentación breve, evita la jerga que solo entienden tus colegas y termina con una pregunta que devuelve la palabra: «Diseño jardines. ¿Y tú?».
teaching.explanationEs: Un pitch cabe en diez segundos; jargon aleja a quien no es del sector.
segments: Keep the pitch short, avoid jargon that only your colleagues understand, and finish with
a question that hands the floor back: 'I design gardens. What about you?'
teaching.audioText: Keep the pitch short, avoid jargon that only your colleagues understand, and finish with a question that hands the floor back: 'I design gardens. What about you?'

teaching.en: A tag such as 'isn't it?' invites agreement when it falls, as in 'It's a lovely venue, isn't it?', but with rising intonation it becomes a real question.
teaching.es: Una coletilla como «isn't it?» busca acuerdo cuando la voz baja, como en «Es un lugar precioso, ¿verdad?», pero con entonación ascendente se convierte en una pregunta real.
teaching.explanationEs: Afirmativa + coletilla negativa; rising intonation pide información, la descendente confirma.
segments: A tag such as 'isn't it?' invites agreement when it falls, as in 'It's
a lovely venue, isn't it?', but with rising intonation it becomes a real question.
teaching.audioText: A tag such as 'isn't it?' invites agreement when it falls, as in 'It's a lovely venue, isn't it?', but with rising intonation it becomes a real question.

teaching.en: When the statement is negative, the tag turns positive, so you say 'You haven't met our host, have you?' and wait to see whether the listener knows her.
teaching.es: Cuando la frase es negativa, la coletilla es positiva, así que dices «Todavía no conoces a nuestra anfitriona, ¿verdad?» y esperas a ver si el oyente la conoce.
teaching.explanationEs: Negativa + coletilla afirmativa: have you?, did they?, can she?
segments: When the statement is negative, the tag turns positive, so you say 'You haven't
met our host, have you?' and wait to see whether the listener knows her.
teaching.audioText: When the statement is negative, the tag turns positive, so you say 'You haven't met our host, have you?' and wait to see whether the listener knows her.

prompt.es: Elige la reescritura que convierte esta presentación plana en memorable.

choices.text: I'm Carlos, a banker with nine years at a large company and a lot of experience.
I'm Carlos, and I work in banking, which is interesting work with many responsibilities.
I'm Carlos, a banker who cooks for forty people every Sunday. What about you?

feedback.es: Solo la primera versión añade un detalle concreto y sorprendente (cocinar para cuarenta personas) y cierra con una pregunta; las demás repiten el currículum.

hint.es: Busca el detalle que sorprende y la pregunta final.

origin.text: Flat introduction: 'Hello, I'm Carlos. I work in banking for a large company, and I have been there for nine years.'

prompt.es: Completa: «Solo Sara intentó destacar, mencionando que pinta barcos los fines de semana.»

feedback.es: Stand out significa destacar entre los demás, y un detalle personal es una buena forma de lograrlo.

hint.es: Es el verbo que forma pareja con «out» para decir destacar.

origin.text: Everyone at the venue introduced themselves with a job title and a company name. Only Sara tried to ___ out, by mentioning that she paints boats at weekends.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Diseño puentes y colecciono relojes viejos. ¿Y tú?»

answer.text: I design bridges and collect old clocks What about you

feedback.es: Ocupación, una rareza personal y la pregunta final que devuelve la palabra, en ese orden.

hint.es: Termina con la pregunta que devuelve la palabra.

prompt.es: Escucha el relato y elige por qué la narradora recuerda al tercer hablante.

choices.text: His strange weekend habit and the question he asked her.
His long list of qualifications as a science teacher at school.
His careful use of special words about his work.

feedback.es: El tercer hablante combina un detalle inesperado (el disfraz de plátano) con una pregunta final; los otros dos solo dieron cargo y jerga.

origin.audio: At the coffee break, three people introduced themselves to me. The first said, I'm a manager at a big company, and then repeated her job title. The second used so much jargon that I lost the thread. The third smiled and said, I'm Leo, I teach science, and on Saturdays I dress up as a giant banana to raise money for a hospital. What about you? I still remember him, although I have forgotten the other two names.

prompt.es: Completa: «Todavía no has probado la sopa, ¿verdad?»

feedback.es: La frase es negativa, así que la coletilla es afirmativa: have you?

origin.text: Tom moved closer across the table and whispered: 'You haven't tried the soup, ___ you?' He was hoping she would say no, so that he could recommend it.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase de presentación con su función.

pairs: I'm Carlos, and I work in banking.
I'm Leo, a teacher who paints boats on Sundays.
What brings you to the conference?
It's a lovely venue, isn't it?

feedback.es: Cada frase tiene su papel: datos sin chispa, un detalle que se recuerda, una pregunta que abre y una coletilla que invita a coincidir.

pairs: I'm Carlos, and I work in banking.
I'm Leo, a teacher who paints boats on Sundays.
What brings you to the conference?
It's a lovely venue, isn't it?

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué reconoce la narradora al final del ejercicio.

choices.text: That the ten-second limit was too strict for anyone to do well.
That her introduction offered him no way into a conversation.
That his job mattered more than his hobby to her.

feedback.es: La narradora admite que su cargo no le dio a Tom nada de lo que preguntar: la presentación plana cerró puertas, la de Tom las abrió.

origin.audio: After the workshop, the organiser asked us to introduce ourselves to a stranger in ten seconds. Mine was flat: I'm Mia, I work in marketing. My partner's was different. He said, I'm Tom, an engineer who builds guitars in his garage, and he asked what had brought me to the workshop. Within a minute we were laughing, and I realised that my job title had given him nothing to ask about.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige qué función cumple la pregunta final de Tom.

choices.text: It gives a second hook about his own job and his hobbies.
It asks her to agree with him about the workshop.
It hands the turn back to her with an open question.

feedback.es: Preguntar qué la llevó al taller devuelve la palabra con una pregunta abierta; no es una coletilla ni otro dato suyo.

origin.audio: After the workshop, the organiser asked us to introduce ourselves to a stranger in ten seconds. Mine was flat: I'm Mia, I work in marketing. My partner's was different. He said, I'm Tom, an engineer who builds guitars in his garage, and he asked what had brought me to the workshop. Within a minute we were laughing, and I realised that my job title had given him nothing to ask about.

prompt.es: Completa: «Era exacta, pero totalmente insulsa, así que añadió que restaura bicicletas.»

feedback.es: Una frase exacta pero sin ningún detalle personal es bland o forgettable: no deja nada que recordar.

origin.text: Sara's first draft read: 'I'm a banker at a large firm.' It was accurate but entirely ___, so she added that she restores old bicycles at weekends.

prompt.es: Escribe tu presentación de diez segundos: gancho y pregunta abierta.

answer.text: I'm Mia, an architect who paints boats in my grandfather's garage at weekends. What brings you to the conference tonight?
accepted: I'm Mia, an architect who paints boats in my grandfather's garage at weekends. What brings you to the conference tonight?
Hi, I am Mia. I'm an architect, and every weekend I paint boats in my grandfather's garage. What about you, what brings you here?
My name is Mia and I'm an architect. At weekends I paint boats in my grandfather's garage. And you, what do you do?

feedback.es: La presentación reúne nombre, ocupación, el gancho de los barcos y una pregunta abierta que devuelve la palabra.

origin.text: Datos: te llamas Mia, eres arquitecta y los fines de semana pintas barcos en el garaje de tu abuelo. Incluye el gancho y termina con una pregunta abierta para el congreso.

prompt.es: Lee el fragmento del artículo y elige la postura del autor sobre las presentaciones.

choices.text: A good introduction invites the listener in rather than performing for them.
Rehearsed pitches are best because they save everyone's time.
A long pause after the question shows that the pitch has failed.

feedback.es: El autor critica los discursos ensayados y propone una invitación: un detalle, una pregunta y una pausa para que el otro responda.

origin.text: The pitch has a bad name, and with reason: most are rehearsed, full of jargon and delivered at speed. The better version is not a speech but an invitation: one surprising detail, one open question, and then a pause in which the other person can answer.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué espera el hablante con la coletilla final.

choices.text: That the listener will explain where the venue is.
That the listener will agree and join in with the chat.
That the listener will admit that the music is too loud.

feedback.es: La coletilla «isn't it?» con la voz que baja busca acuerdo y abre la conversación; después añade una pregunta concreta.

origin.audio: Lovely venue, isn't it? I wasn't sure about the music at first, but the food more than makes up for it. Have you tried the little fish pies yet?

prompt.es: Completa: «Su presentación estaba tan llena de jerga que nadie entendió qué hacía.»

feedback.es: Jargon es el lenguaje técnico que solo entiende el sector: aleja a quien escucha en lugar de acercarlo.

origin.text: Five minutes into the evening, the new manager was still talking. His introduction was so full of ___ that nobody could tell what he actually did.

es: Distinguir en un audio si una persona muestra interés genuino o solo cortesía a partir de ecos, reacciones breves, tono y respuestas evasivas, y justificar la decisión con dos pistas.

teaching.en: An echo question repeats part of what you heard with a rising tone, as in 'You moved to Quito?', and it tells the speaker that you want to hear the rest.
teaching.es: Una pregunta eco repite parte de lo que oíste con tono ascendente, como en «¿Te mudaste a Quito?», y le dice al hablante que quieres oír el resto.
teaching.explanationEs: El eco sube al final y pide que el otro amplíe: es una señal de interés.
segments: An echo question repeats part of what you heard with a rising tone, as in 'You
moved to Quito?', and it tells the speaker that you want to hear the rest.
teaching.audioText: An echo question repeats part of what you heard with a rising tone, as in 'You moved to Quito?', and it tells the speaker that you want to hear the rest.

teaching.en: An enthusiastic voice rises and falls and speeds up at the exciting parts, whereas a flat voice stays on one note, however polite the words may be.
teaching.es: Una voz entusiasta sube, baja y se acelera en las partes emocionantes, mientras que una voz plana se queda en una sola nota, por muy corteses que sean las palabras.
teaching.explanationEs: El tono cuenta tanto como las palabras: flat es sin altibajos.
segments: An enthusiastic voice rises and falls and speeds up at the exciting parts, whereas
a flat voice stays on one note, however polite the words may be.
teaching.audioText: An enthusiastic voice rises and falls and speeds up at the exciting parts, whereas a flat voice stays on one note, however polite the words may be.

teaching.en: When a person hesitates before answering, or gives a perfunctory 'Mm, right', the interest may be nothing more than courtesy rather than a wish to continue.
teaching.es: Cuando una persona duda antes de responder o suelta un «Mm, claro» mecánico, el interés puede ser solo cortesía y no ganas de continuar.
teaching.explanationEs: Perfunctory = hecho por cumplir; courtesy = cortesía: hacer lo correcto sin interés real.
segments: When a person hesitates before answering, or gives a perfunctory 'Mm, right', the
interest may be nothing more than courtesy rather than a wish to continue.
teaching.audioText: When a person hesitates before answering, or gives a perfunctory 'Mm, right', the interest may be nothing more than courtesy rather than a wish to continue.

teaching.en: 'That's interesting' can be a lukewarm reply, and a noncommittal 'We'll see' is similar, so you have to read between the lines instead of trusting the words alone.
teaching.es: «Qué interesante» puede ser una respuesta tibia, y un evasivo «Ya veremos» es parecido, así que debes leer entre líneas en vez de fiarte solo de las palabras.
teaching.explanationEs: Lukewarm = poco entusiasta; noncommittal = sin comprometerse; read between the lines = deducir lo no dicho.
segments: 'That's interesting' can be a lukewarm reply, and a noncommittal 'We'll see' is similar,
so you have to read between the lines instead of trusting the words alone.
teaching.audioText: 'That's interesting' can be a lukewarm reply, and a noncommittal 'We'll see' is similar, so you have to read between the lines instead of trusting the words alone.

teaching.en: An eager listener will nod, lean forward and ask for more, and these small signals often count for more than anything said aloud.
teaching.es: Un oyente ansioso por saber más asentirá, se inclinará hacia delante y pedirá más, y estas pequeñas señales suelen pesar más que cualquier frase.
teaching.explanationEs: Eager indica ganas de saber más; nod es asentir con la cabeza.
segments: An eager listener will nod, lean forward and ask for more, and
these small signals often count for more than anything said aloud.
teaching.audioText: An eager listener will nod, lean forward and ask for more, and these small signals often count for more than anything said aloud.

teaching.en: A bored listener looks at the clock, sighs and gives one-word answers, yet a shy but keen listener may also go quiet, so never decide from a single clue.
teaching.es: Un oyente aburrido mira el reloj, suspira y responde con una palabra, pero uno tímido y aun así interesado también puede callarse, así que nunca decidas por una sola pista.
teaching.explanationEs: Bored describe cómo se siente el oyente; boring, lo que le resulta aburrido.
segments: A bored listener looks at the clock, sighs and gives one-word answers, yet a shy
but keen listener may also go quiet, so never decide from a single clue.
teaching.audioText: A bored listener looks at the clock, sighs and gives one-word answers, yet a shy but keen listener may also go quiet, so never decide from a single clue.

prompt.es: Decide qué muestra el segundo hablante con sus dos primeras preguntas.

choices.text: Real interest: he repeats the news and asks for the reason.
Polite distance: he repeats the news to close the topic.
Surprise at a plan that he thinks is a very bad idea.

feedback.es: Repetir el dato con subida y preguntar el motivo son las marcas del interés genuino; ninguna de las dos frases cierra el tema ni critica el plan.

hint.es: Mira si la repetición va seguida de una pregunta de detalle.

origin.text: First speaker: 'I finally left my job last month and moved to Quito.' Second speaker: 'You moved to Quito? On your own? What made you choose it?'

prompt.es: Completa: «Sus respuestas eran tan evasivas que no supe si estaba contenta.»

feedback.es: Noncommittal describe respuestas que no se comprometen con nada: ni sí, ni no, ni interés claro.

hint.es: Es el adjetivo de «Ya veremos»: no se compromete.

origin.text: Her replies were so ___ that I could not tell whether she was pleased or simply being polite. She said 'Mm, we'll see' twice without asking a single question.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Asintió con entusiasmo y le pidió que le contara más.»

answer.text: She nodded eagerly and asked him to tell her more

feedback.es: El asentimiento y la petición de más detalles son las dos pistas de interés genuino que se suman en esta frase.

hint.es: Empieza con el gesto y termina con la petición.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige la pista que más claramente muestra el interés de Ana.

choices.text: Her brief praise followed by a polite change of the subject.
Her echoes and her follow-up question about the hardest night.
Her silence while she nodded and looked at the floor.

feedback.es: Ana repite los datos, pregunta por la peor noche y reacciona con voz animada: eso es interés genuino, no un elogio de pasada.

origin.audio: At the party, I told Ana that I had walked across the Andes in twenty days. She did not just say, how nice. She said, twenty days? On foot? Did you carry everything yourself? Then she leaned towards me and asked what had been the hardest night. Her voice went up at the surprising parts, and she kept nodding. By the end I had told her about the storm, the guide's broken radio and the dog that followed us for three days.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada respuesta con lo que suele indicar.

pairs: You climbed it alone?
Mm. Sure. Right.
Wow! And how did you start?
We'll see... I suppose so.

feedback.es: El eco, la pregunta de detalle y la reacción animada suman interés; los sonidos secos y las evasivas lo restan.

pairs: You climbed it alone?
Mm. Sure. Right.
Wow! And how did you start?
We'll see... I suppose so.

prompt.es: Lee la escena y elige qué sugiere la reacción de la colega.

choices.text: Enthusiasm that she prefers to hide from the others
A wish to hear more on another day
Polite patience rather than real curiosity about it

feedback.es: Un «interesting» plano, sin mirar y sin ninguna pregunta, apunta a paciencia cortés, no a curiosidad.

origin.text: Leo spent five minutes describing his new project. His colleague replied, without looking up: 'That's interesting. Hmm. Sounds like a lot of work.' Then she asked him nothing and went back to her screen.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué se deduce del final de este encuentro en el ascensor.

choices.text: The second colleague was only polite, so the first drops the topic.
The second colleague liked the news but was in a hurry to leave.
The first colleague was offended and decided to avoid her from then on.

feedback.es: La pausa, la mirada al móvil y el «interesting» sin preguntas indican cortesía; por eso la primera colega deja el tema.

origin.audio: Two colleagues meet in the lift. One says, I've just got three new cats. The other pauses, says, oh, nice, and looks at her phone. Right, she adds, that's interesting. Well, this is my floor. The first colleague says, lovely to chat, but she decides not to mention the cats again.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige las dos pistas que justifican esa conclusión.

choices.text: The word nice and the wish that they chat again.
The pause and the glance at her phone.
The mention of the cats and the floor number.

feedback.es: La duda inicial y la mirada al móvil son pistas de desinterés; «nice» es solo una palabra amable y el piso es una simple excusa.

origin.audio: Two colleagues meet in the lift. One says, I've just got three new cats. The other pauses, says, oh, nice, and looks at her phone. Right, she adds, that's interesting. Well, this is my floor. The first colleague says, lovely to chat, but she decides not to mention the cats again.

prompt.es: Completa: «Si lees entre líneas, esperaba que la conversación terminara pronto.»

feedback.es: Read between the lines es deducir lo que alguien piensa sin decirlo, a partir de pausas, dudas y falta de preguntas.

origin.text: Her words were perfectly polite, but if you read between the ___, she was hoping the conversation would end soon. She had hesitated twice and never asked a question.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Una respuesta tibia sin pregunta rara vez muestra interés real.»

answer.text: A lukewarm reply without a question rarely shows real interest

feedback.es: La frase resume la regla de la clase: sin pregunta de detalle, una reacción tibia no basta para hablar de interés.

prompt.es: Lee el mensaje del foro y elige cuál es la preocupación principal del autor.

choices.text: Whether his ideas are too long to explain in a meeting.
Whether his manager has already rejected his proposal.
Whether the polite reactions of his new team hide a lack of real interest.

feedback.es: El autor duda de si el «Interesting!» sin seguimiento y el asentimiento de su jefa son cortesía o interés; no habla de longitud ni de un rechazo.

origin.text: My new team always says 'Interesting!' when I share an idea, but nobody ever follows up. Is that a polite way of saying no, or is it simply how they speak? Last week my manager nodded for ten minutes and then said she would think about it. I honestly cannot read her at all.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué efecto busca el hablante con «Go on».

choices.text: To invite the traveller to continue with the story.
To stop the traveller from going into too much detail.
To change the subject to the radio.

feedback.es: «Go on, I want to hear everything» anima al otro a seguir, y las preguntas que siguen lo confirman.

origin.audio: Wow, you crossed the sea alone for a week? With no radio? Go on, I want to hear everything. Was it lonely, or did you get used to it after a few days?

prompt.es: Completa: «Un gesto y una sonrisa pueden ser mera cortesía.»

feedback.es: Courtesy es la cortesía que se ofrece por educación: un gesto la muestra, pero una pregunta de seguimiento exige interés real.

origin.text: After ten minutes of one-word answers, it was clear that he was only being polite. A nod and a smile can be nothing but ___, but a follow-up question is much harder to pretend.

es: Sostener una charla de ocho turnos con desconocidos combinando ecos, preguntas de seguimiento abiertas y aportaciones personales breves, sin fisgonear ni divagar.

vocabulary.es: apoyarse en, desarrollar a partir de

teaching.en: A follow-up question picks up one detail the other person has just mentioned and invites them to elaborate, which shows that you were really listening.
teaching.es: Una pregunta de seguimiento recoge un detalle que el otro acaba de mencionar y le invita a ampliarlo, lo que demuestra que estabas escuchando de verdad.
teaching.explanationEs: Elaborate = dar más detalles; la pregunta parte de algo que ya dijo.
segments: A follow-up question picks up one detail the other person has just mentioned
and invites them to elaborate, which shows that you were really listening.
teaching.audioText: A follow-up question picks up one detail the other person has just mentioned and invites them to elaborate, which shows that you were really listening.

teaching.en: Do not pry into money, age or politics with someone you have just met; an open-ended question about their work or travels is far less intrusive.
teaching.es: No fisgonees en dinero, edad o política con alguien que acabas de conocer; una pregunta abierta sobre su trabajo o sus viajes es mucho menos invasiva.
teaching.explanationEs: Pry es preguntar cosas demasiado privadas; una open-ended question no se contesta con sí o no.
segments: Do not pry into money, age or politics with someone you have just
met; an open-ended question about their work or travels is far less intrusive.
teaching.audioText: Do not pry into money, age or politics with someone you have just met; an open-ended question about their work or travels is far less intrusive.

teaching.en: When she shares something personal, reciprocate with a detail of similar size, so that the chat keeps a healthy give and take instead of becoming an interview.
teaching.es: Cuando ella comparte algo personal, corresponde con un detalle de tamaño parecido, para que la charla mantenga un buen equilibrio y no se convierta en una entrevista.
teaching.explanationEs: Reciprocate mantiene el equilibrio: ni solo escuchas ni solo hablas.
segments: When she shares something personal, reciprocate with a detail of similar size, so that
the chat keeps a healthy give and take instead of becoming an interview.
teaching.audioText: When she shares something personal, reciprocate with a detail of similar size, so that the chat keeps a healthy give and take instead of becoming an interview.

teaching.en: A short tangent is fine, but bring the conversation back to its thread: 'Anyway, you were telling me about Manta and the fishing boat.'
teaching.es: Una digresión breve está bien, pero vuelve al hilo: «En fin, me estabas contando lo de Manta y el barco de pesca».
teaching.explanationEs: Tangent es salirse del tema; «Anyway, you were saying…» te devuelve a él.
segments: A short tangent is fine, but bring the conversation back to its
thread: 'Anyway, you were telling me about Manta and the fishing boat.'
teaching.audioText: A short tangent is fine, but bring the conversation back to its thread: 'Anyway, you were telling me about Manta and the fishing boat.'

teaching.en: If you ramble for a full minute, the other person can only wait, so keep each turn short, build on her last sentence and keep the ball rolling with another question.
teaching.es: Si divagas durante un minuto entero, el otro solo puede esperar, así que mantén cada turno corto, apóyate en su última frase y mantén viva la charla con otra pregunta.
teaching.explanationEs: Ramble es hablar sin punto claro; build on = partir de lo que dijo el otro.
segments: If you ramble for a full minute, the other person can only wait, so keep each
turn short, build on her last sentence and keep the ball rolling with another question.
teaching.audioText: If you ramble for a full minute, the other person can only wait, so keep each turn short, build on her last sentence and keep the ball rolling with another question.

teaching.en: As soon as a quiet guest begins to open up, resist the urge to fill every pause and give her room to elaborate on the story.
teaching.es: En cuanto un invitado callado empieza a abrirse, resiste la tentación de llenar cada pausa y déjale espacio para que amplíe la historia.
teaching.explanationEs: Open up = empezar a contar cosas personales; el silencio breve ayuda.
segments: As soon as a quiet guest begins to open up, resist the urge
to fill every pause and give her room to elaborate on the story.
teaching.audioText: As soon as a quiet guest begins to open up, resist the urge to fill every pause and give her room to elaborate on the story.

prompt.es: Elige la mejor pregunta de seguimiento para el comentario de Leo.

choices.text: Did your family have a lot of money in Manta?
By the sea? What was it like growing up there?
I grew up by a lake, and it was much bigger.

feedback.es: La pregunta abierta recoge el detalle del mar y pide que lo amplíe; preguntar por dinero es indiscreto y hablar de tu lago es una digresión.

hint.es: Debe aprovechar el detalle que acaba de decir y no ser indiscreta.

origin.text: Mia has just met Leo at a wedding. He says: 'I grew up by the sea in Manta, and I still miss the noise of the waves at night.'

prompt.es: Completa: «Tom decidió corresponder con una breve historia de su propia familia.»

feedback.es: Reciprocate es devolver el gesto con una aportación de tamaño parecido, para que la charla no sea un interrogatorio.

hint.es: Es el verbo de devolver el gesto con algo equivalente.

origin.text: When Ana mentioned her brother's wedding, Tom decided to ___ with a short story about his own family, so that the chat stayed balanced.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Mencionaste una panadería, ¿cómo la empezaste?»

answer.text: You mentioned a bakery so how did you start it

feedback.es: La pregunta de seguimiento cita primero el detalle mencionado y después pide que se amplíe.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige la diferencia que marca la narradora entre sus dos vecinos de mesa.

choices.text: One neighbour talked about himself all evening, the other about her flat.
One neighbour asked about her family, the other about her job.
One neighbour asked intrusive questions, the other picked up on a detail.

feedback.es: El hombre acumula preguntas privadas; la mujer recoge un detalle («you grew up in Cuenca?») y pide ampliarlo: eso es interés, no fisgoneo.

origin.audio: At dinner I sat next to a man who asked how much my flat cost, whether I was married and what I earned, all within five minutes. Each time I answered briefly, he moved on to something more personal. Then a woman on my other side said, you grew up in Cuenca? What was that like? I talked about the river for ten minutes without noticing the time. Only later did I understand the difference between prying and showing interest.

prompt.es: Completa: «Es fácil divagar durante minutos sobre tus propias noticias.»

feedback.es: Ramble on es seguir hablando sin un punto claro; la solución son turnos cortos y una pregunta final.

origin.text: It is easy to ___ on for minutes about your own news. A good speaker gives two or three sentences, then turns to the other person with a question.

prompt.es: Lee el intercambio y elige qué le falta para sostener una conversación.

choices.text: Follow-up questions that build on each answer
A polite closing before the long silence begins
A change of topic to something lighter

feedback.es: Cada respuesta se queda en una palabra y nadie recoge un detalle: faltan ecos y preguntas de seguimiento que amplíen lo dicho.

origin.text: 'So what do you do?' 'I'm an engineer.' 'Right.' 'And you?' 'A nurse.' 'Nice.' After that, the two of them said nothing more and looked at the dessert table.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige cómo mantiene Ana el equilibrio de la charla.

choices.text: She tells a longer story about Manta and stops asking questions.
She offers a matching detail and then asks another question.
She repeats his words but never shares anything of her own.

feedback.es: Ana corresponde con un dato suyo (dejó Manta a los dieciocho) y enseguida pregunta por la playa: aporta y devuelve la palabra.

origin.audio: Carlos told Ana that he had moved to Quito for work. Ana repeated, to Quito? and asked what he missed most about home. He said the sea, and, without thinking, she added that she had left Manta at eighteen and still dreamed of the waves. Then she asked whether he had found a beach near the capital. Carlos laughed and said there was none, but a friend had taken him to a lake.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige qué sugiere la pregunta de Ana sobre la playa.

choices.text: She is trying to change the subject away from the sea.
She doubts that Carlos really misses the sea.
She is building on what he said about missing the sea.

feedback.es: La pregunta parte de lo que Carlos acaba de decir (echa de menos el mar): es seguimiento, no un cambio de tema ni una duda.

origin.audio: Carlos told Ana that he had moved to Quito for work. Ana repeated, to Quito? and asked what he missed most about home. He said the sea, and, without thinking, she added that she had left Manta at eighteen and still dreamed of the waves. Then she asked whether he had found a beach near the capital. Carlos laughed and said there was none, but a friend had taken him to a lake.

prompt.es: Completa: «Sabía mantener viva la conversación con un comentario y una pregunta.»

feedback.es: Keep the ball rolling significa mantener viva la conversación, aquí con un comentario corto y una pregunta sobre lo dicho.

origin.text: Nobody at our table knew each other, but Leo was good at small talk. He knew how to keep the ___ rolling: a short comment, then a question about something the other person had just said.

prompt.es: Escribe ocho turnos de charla en una boda, con un eco y dos preguntas de seguimiento.

answer.text: Sara: So, how do you know the bride? Tom: We played football together at school. And you? Sara: I am her cousin. You played football? Tom: Yes, until I hurt my leg at sixteen, and then I found cooking. What do you do, Sara? Sara: I am an architect, and last year I restored an old theatre in Cuenca. Tom: A theatre? How did you get that job? Sara: I wrote to the mayor every week for a year, and he finally gave in. Did you become a cook after the injury? Tom: Not at once. I worked in banking for fifteen years, but I never stopped cooking, and at forty I opened a small bakery. Sara: That is brave. What was the hardest part? Tom: Getting up at four every morning! Shall we find the cake?

Tom: How do you know the bride? Sara: We studied together at university. And you? Tom: She is my cousin. You studied together? Sara: Yes, and now I am an architect. Last year I restored an old theatre in Cuenca. What about you, Tom? Tom: A theatre? How did you start? Sara: I wrote to the mayor every week for a year until he agreed. What do you do? Tom: I was a banker for fifteen years, but at forty I opened a small bakery. Sara: A bakery? What was the hardest part? Tom: Getting up at four every morning! I still bake bread for the whole street. Sara: That is lovely. Shall we go and find some cake? Tom: Good idea.

feedback.es: La conversación alterna ecos, aportaciones breves y preguntas de seguimiento sobre detalles que cada uno mencionó.

origin.text: Datos: Sara (arquitecta, restauró un teatro viejo en Cuenca) y Tom (banquero durante quince años; a los cuarenta abrió una panadería). Empieza con cómo conocen a la novia. Incluye un eco, dos preguntas de seguimiento y una aportación personal breve de cada uno.

prompt.es: Lee el fragmento de la columnista y elige qué criterio propone para no fisgonear.

choices.text: Whether the question leaves the other person free to choose how much to share.
Whether the topic is connected with money, age or politics.
Whether the question comes early in the conversation.

feedback.es: La autora aclara que el problema no es el tema, sino que la pregunta deje al otro decidir cuánto contar.

origin.text: Asking how much someone earns is prying, but asking what they enjoy about their work is an invitation. The difference is not the topic itself: it is whether the question leaves the other person free to decide how much to reveal.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige con qué fin dice el hablante «Anyway, you were telling me…».

choices.text: To end the chat before she has time to finish her story.
To return to her story after a tangent of his own.
To blame her for stopping in the middle.

feedback.es: Tras una digresión sobre su perro, el hablante vuelve al hilo de la otra persona: así devuelve el turno y retoma su historia.

origin.audio: Sorry, I have been talking about my dog for ages. Anyway, you were telling me about Manta, and you stopped halfway through the story about the fishing boat.

prompt.es: Completa: «La pregunta de Tom no pretendía fisgonear: solo quería saber más.»

feedback.es: Pry es preguntar con indiscreción; aquí la pregunta es abierta y deja a ella decidir cuánto responder.

origin.text: Tom's question was not meant to ___: he simply wanted to know more about her work, and she was free to answer as little as she liked.

es: Abrir una conversación, crear afinidad, cerrarla y redactar un mensaje de seguimiento cordial con recordatorio, detalle, propuesta concreta, salida fácil y despedida.

usesVocabulary: pick up where we left off

vocabulary.es: ponerse al día, retomar el contacto

vocabulary.en: pick up where we left off

teaching.en: A vague message like 'Let's keep in touch' rarely leads to a second meeting, because it leaves the other person to work out what you actually want.
teaching.es: Un mensaje vago como «Mantengámonos en contacto» rara vez lleva a un segundo encuentro, porque deja al otro la tarea de adivinar qué quieres realmente.
teaching.explanationEs: Vague es lo contrario de concrete: sin día, hora ni plan.
segments: A vague message like 'Let's keep in touch' rarely leads to a second meeting,
because it leaves the other person to work out what you actually want.
teaching.audioText: A vague message like 'Let's keep in touch' rarely leads to a second meeting, because it leaves the other person to work out what you actually want.

teaching.en: Remind the person who you are and why you reach out, perhaps naming a mutual acquaintance: 'We met at the wedding, by the cake table.'
teaching.es: Recuerda a la persona quién eres y por qué le escribes, quizá nombrando a un conocido en común: «Nos conocimos en la boda, junto a la mesa de los postres».
teaching.explanationEs: Reach out es contactar con alguien; remind + persona + dato que lo ubique.
segments: Remind the person who you are and why you reach out, perhaps naming
a mutual acquaintance: 'We met at the wedding, by the cake table.'
teaching.audioText: Remind the person who you are and why you reach out, perhaps naming a mutual acquaintance: 'We met at the wedding, by the cake table.'

teaching.en: A quick recap of one detail shows that you listened, and it lets you touch base without sounding like a salesman or a stranger.
teaching.es: Un breve resumen de un detalle demuestra que escuchaste, y te permite retomar el contacto sin sonar como un vendedor ni como un extraño.
teaching.explanationEs: Recap: menciona algo que dijo («You said you were training for a marathon»).
segments: A quick recap of one detail shows that you listened, and it
lets you touch base without sounding like a salesman or a stranger.
teaching.audioText: A quick recap of one detail shows that you listened, and it lets you touch base without sounding like a salesman or a stranger.

teaching.en: Then propose something concrete: 'Would you like to have coffee next Thursday at ten, so that we can pick up where we left off?'
teaching.es: Después propón algo concreto: «¿Te apetece tomar un café el próximo jueves a las diez, para que retomemos donde lo dejamos?».
teaching.explanationEs: Concrete = día, hora y plan; en inglés se dice «have coffee», no «take a coffee».
segments: Then propose something concrete: 'Would you like to have coffee next Thursday
at ten, so that we can pick up where we left off?'
teaching.audioText: Then propose something concrete: 'Would you like to have coffee next Thursday at ten, so that we can pick up where we left off?'

teaching.en: When the other person suggests something, you can answer 'I'd love to take you up on that', and a gentle nudge a week later is perfectly acceptable.
teaching.es: Cuando la otra persona sugiere algo, puedes contestar «Me encantaría aceptar tu invitación», y un suave recordatorio una semana después es perfectamente aceptable.
teaching.explanationEs: Take you up on = aceptar una oferta; nudge es un recordatorio educado, nunca una presión.
segments: When the other person suggests something, you can answer 'I'd love to take you
up on that', and a gentle nudge a week later is perfectly acceptable.
teaching.audioText: When the other person suggests something, you can answer 'I'd love to take you up on that', and a gentle nudge a week later is perfectly acceptable.

teaching.en: End with a low-pressure sign-off such as 'Warm regards', and remind the other person that saying no is fine: 'No worries if you are busy.'
teaching.es: Termina con una despedida sin presión, como «Un saludo cordial», y recuerda al otro que puede decir que no: «No pasa nada si estás ocupado».
teaching.explanationEs: El sign-off cierra el mensaje; la salida fácil quita presión y hace más probable un sí.
segments: End with a low-pressure sign-off such as 'Warm regards', and remind the other
person that saying no is fine: 'No worries if you are busy.'
teaching.audioText: End with a low-pressure sign-off such as 'Warm regards', and remind the other person that saying no is fine: 'No worries if you are busy.'

prompt.es: Elige el mensaje que combina recordatorio, detalle y propuesta concreta.

choices.text: Hi Tom, it was lovely to meet you at the book fair. Let's keep in touch, and perhaps we can meet some time when we are both free to do so.
Hi Tom, I am writing to formally request a meeting at your earliest convenience concerning volunteers for your theatre group.
Hi Tom, we met at the book fair by the coffee stand. You mentioned your theatre group needs volunteers, so could we meet on Friday at five?

feedback.es: Solo el primer mensaje sitúa dónde se conocieron, retoma el detalle de los voluntarios y propone día y hora; los otros son vagos o demasiado rígidos.

hint.es: Busca día, hora y un detalle de la charla.

origin.text: Mia wants to write to a man she met at a book fair. He had said that his small theatre group needs volunteers for the autumn show.

prompt.es: Completa: «Te escribo para ponerme en contacto tras nuestra charla en la boda.»

feedback.es: Reach out significa ponerse en contacto con alguien, y es el verbo habitual para abrir un mensaje de seguimiento.

hint.es: Es el verbo que acompaña a «out» para contactar.

origin.text: It was lovely to meet you at the wedding on Saturday. I am writing to ___ out after our chat, because I would love to continue the conversation over coffee.

prompt.es: Ordena: «¿Te apetece tomar un café el próximo jueves a las diez?»

answer.text: Would you like to have coffee next Thursday at ten

feedback.es: La propuesta concreta usa «Would you like to» y da el día y la hora.

hint.es: Empieza con la fórmula de invitación.

prompt.es: Escucha el mensaje de voz y elige qué propone Tom y cómo deja una salida fácil.

choices.text: A first guitar lesson on Saturday, with another date if needed.
A guitar concert on Saturday, with a refund if you need it.
A weekly class from next month, with no other option.

feedback.es: Tom propone una primera clase el sábado a las once y ofrece otra fecha si no le conviene: propuesta concreta más salida fácil.

origin.audio: Hi Ana, it's Tom, from the wedding, the one who dropped a glass of juice beside the cake table. You mentioned that you were looking for a teacher for your cousin's guitar lessons, and I happen to give lessons on Saturdays. Would you like to try a first session with her this Saturday at eleven? There is no pressure, of course, and if the date does not suit you, just tell me and we will find another one.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase del mensaje con la función que cumple.

pairs: I'm the one who lost an umbrella at the fair.
You said the trains to Cuenca are always late.
Shall we meet on Friday at noon?
No pressure if the week is full.

feedback.es: Cada frase cumple una función distinta: identificarte, demostrar atención, proponer un plan y quitar presión.

prompt.es: Lee el borrador y elige su problema principal.

choices.text: It is too formal for a message between two guests.
It is too vague to lead to a second meeting.
It is too long to be read in a single go.

feedback.es: No da día, lugar ni detalle de la charla: «some time» y «call me maybe» dejan al otro sin nada que responder.

origin.text: 'Hey! Loved the party. We should meet up some time, call me maybe. Bye!' Mia sent this to a man she had talked to for an hour, and she never received an answer.

prompt.es: Lee el correo de Mia y elige qué pretende con su doble oferta.

choices.text: To test how keen Leo really is about his marathon training.
To avoid having to name a day for the meeting herself.
To make replying easy by offering two light options.

feedback.es: Ofrecer enviar el artículo o tomar un café baja el esfuerzo de responder; además Mia sí concreta día y hora, y cierra con «No worries».

origin.text: Hi Leo, it's Mia from Ana and Tom's wedding. You said you were training for a marathon, so I thought you might like the article I mentioned. Shall I send it by email, or would you prefer to have coffee next Thursday at ten, and I can bring a printed copy? No worries either way.

prompt.es: Escucha el mensaje de voz y elige por qué será difícil responder.

choices.text: It gives no day, place or plan that he can accept.
It is so formal that he will not feel able to answer.
It asks for a reply so soon that he has no time.

feedback.es: Todo son «some time», «maybe» y «at some point»: sin propuesta concreta, el oyente no tiene nada a lo que contestar.

origin.audio: Hi, it's Sara, from the book fair. It was really nice to meet you. We should get together some time, maybe, whenever you are free. Anyway, let's keep in touch, and I'll be in touch at some point. Take care.

prompt.es: Completa: «Me encantaría aceptar tu invitación a ese café la semana que viene.»

feedback.es: Take you up on es aceptar una oferta o invitación que otro ha hecho, y es más natural que «accept your invitation».

origin.text: Thank you for a lovely evening, and for mentioning that little café near the station. I'd love to ___ you up on that coffee next week, as long as Thursday still works.

prompt.es: Redacta el mensaje de seguimiento a Leo con recordatorio, detalle, propuesta y despedida.

answer.text: Hi Leo, it's Mia from Ana and Tom's wedding. We met by the cake table, and I hope you don't mind me getting in touch. I have been thinking about our chat ever since. You said you were training for a marathon and that you were looking for someone to run with in the mornings, so I wanted to reach out. I have also found the article about training that I mentioned, and I would be happy to send it to you. Would you like to have coffee next Thursday at ten, at the café in the square? We could pick up where we left off and talk about the route. No worries at all if you are busy, and feel free to suggest another day. Either way, it was great chatting with you. Warm regards, Mia

Hello Leo, this is Mia, and we met at the wedding of Ana and Tom, by the cake table. I really enjoyed our chat about your marathon training, and I remembered that you want a partner for your morning runs. I have found the article about training that I promised you, so I can send it to you whenever you like. Would you like to have coffee next Thursday at 10 in the café on the square? That way we could pick up where we left off and plan a first run together. No problem at all if the week is too busy for you, we can easily find another day. Thank you again for the lovely conversation. Best wishes, Mia

feedback.es: El mensaje recuerda el lugar, retoma el maratón y las carreras matinales, cumple la promesa del artículo, propone día y hora concretos y deja una salida fácil con una despedida cordial.

origin.text: Datos: conociste a Leo en la boda de Ana y Tom, junto a la mesa de los postres. Entrena para un maratón y busca compañía para correr por las mañanas; le prometiste enviarle un artículo sobre entrenamiento. Propón un café el próximo jueves a las 10 en el café de la plaza, deja una salida fácil y despídete con calidez.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige con qué fin habla Leo de un «gentle nudge».

choices.text: To cancel the coffee plans and blame the busy week.
To remind her politely and leave the choice to her.
To insist that she must decide by Thursday at the latest.

feedback.es: Un nudge es un recordatorio suave: Leo retoma el plan, dice «no pressure» y ofrece otra fecha, sin cancelar ni exigir.

origin.audio: Hi Mia, Leo here. Just a gentle nudge about the coffee we mentioned. I know the week has been busy, so no pressure at all. If Thursday is still too soon, I am free on Saturday morning, and I can meet you at any place that suits you best.

prompt.es: Lee el borrador y elige la despedida que mejor encaja con su registro.

choices.text: Cheers, see you around!
Yours faithfully, Miss Mia
Kind regards, Mia

feedback.es: El mensaje es cordial y semiformal: «Kind regards» encaja; «Cheers» es demasiado informal y «Yours faithfully» demasiado rígido para alguien a quien ya conoces.

origin.text: Dear Dr Sol, it was lovely to meet you at the conference. I enjoyed our conversation about rural clinics and would love to hear more. Would you be free for a short call next week? If not, I completely understand. ___

prompt.es: Completa: «Conviene retomar la charla donde la dejamos: menciona primero el maratón.»

feedback.es: Pick up where we left off es retomar la conversación en el punto donde se interrumpió, que es lo que hace un buen seguimiento.

origin.text: You don't have to start from nothing in your message. It is better to pick ___ where you left off: mention the marathon first and then make your proposal.
